_comment: Feature 47 (Swagger / OpenAPI). Written 2026-08-06 from a measured four-way audit; MOVED owed->proven 2026-08-07 once a named swagger_contract suite existed in all four frameworks (tests/test_swagger_contract.py, tests/SwaggerContractTest.php, spec/swagger_contract_spec.rb, test/swaggerContract.test.ts). Each suite fetches the real /swagger/openapi.json over a real socket (no mocks), validates it with a real OpenAPI validator declared test-only (the frameworks stay zero runtime-dependency), and each of the 10 assertions is proven a real gate by mutation. Node's generator dropped typed path params (fixed here); the other three shipped all 10 invariants correctly. The originating audit found TWO OF FOUR shipped a structurally invalid document; that is now gated in all four. EXTENDED 2026-08-13 (SWAG-DEC-01/02, OWNER-DECISIONS.md 2026-08-11) with 3 more invariants (10->13): Node's spec regenerated per request but over a boot-time router.getRoutes() snapshot (fixed, live routes now); Node's /__feedback/* was excluded only by boot ordering, not by its exclusion list, so a shared 8-prefix internal-exclusion list now backs all four frameworks (python/ruby/node widened from /swagger+/__dev only; php already carried it); the per-operation shape (401/summary/tags/description) is now gated identical across all four (python added the 401 + summary/tags defaults it was missing, ruby dropped its always-on empty description). All 13 proven by mutation in every framework named below.

invariants.rule: The document fetched from /swagger/openapi.json passes a real OpenAPI validator for the version it declares, in every framework, for an app with routes, path params, a model and a secured route.
invariants.why: MEASURED 2026-08-06 with openapi-spec-validator: python VALID, php INVALID, ruby VALID, node INVALID. Nothing anywhere validated the generated output, which is why two frameworks shipped a document no spec-compliant client or gateway can consume. This is the invariant that would have caught BOTH P1s below on its own, so it is the one worth building first. It needs a validator, which is a test-only dependency - the frameworks stay zero-dep.

invariants.rule: Every {name} in a path key has a matching parameter entry with in:path and required:true, and the path key itself carries no framework type token.
invariants.why: MEASURED: Node emitted NO in:path parameter anywhere, unconditionally - the framework registers /__frond/live/{name} itself, so an app with zero user routes already published an invalid document. Root cause: extractPathParams matched the FILE-SYSTEM spelling [id] while routeDiscovery converts [id] to {id} before a route is registered, so the regex never matched at runtime. PHP separately leaked the token into the key ('/api/typed/{id:int}') and declared no parameter for it. FIXED in both (tina4-nodejs f217a5e, tina4-php 5a4f838d) with the whole-document form of this rule asserted in test/swaggerPathParams.test.ts and tests/SwaggerTypedPathParamTest.php. OWED because Python and Ruby have no equivalent suite - they were already correct, which is exactly the state in which a regression goes unnoticed.

invariants.rule: An operation's `security` is derived from the same flag dispatch enforces, never a parallel one. A route the server answers 401 for is documented as requiring auth; a route explicitly opened is documented as public.
invariants.why: MEASURED: POST /api/items with no Authorization header returned 401 in all four, but Ruby's document carried no security key at all - the write API was documented public while being enforced. Ruby carries two flags and Swagger read the wrong one: router.rb sets auth_required (what dispatch enforces, flipped by .secure/.no_auth) while swagger.rb branched on auth_handler, which defaults to nil. Every write route registered the ordinary way was affected, AutoCrud included, and .secure on a GET never reached the document. FIXED in tina4-ruby 665151d with spec/swagger_security_mirrors_gate_spec.rb (positive, .secure GET, and the .no_auth negative). OWED because Python, PHP and Node have no equivalent suite.

invariants.rule: The same typed route token maps to the same JSON Schema fragment in all four: int/integer -> integer, float/number -> number, uuid -> string+format uuid, slug/alpha/alnum -> string+pattern, bare -> string. An unknown token degrades to string rather than dropping the parameter.
invariants.why: MEASURED: python emitted {"type":"integer"} for a declared int, php emitted no parameter at all, ruby emitted integer, node emitted nothing. Python's _PARAM_TYPE_SCHEMA is the reference and PHP now mirrors it over exactly the token set Router::compilePath accepts. A generated client's argument type comes from this, so a divergence here is a divergence in every downstream SDK.

invariants.rule: An ORM model becomes ONE components.schemas entry keyed by the model CLASS name, with `required` derived from nullability, referenced by $ref rather than inlined.
invariants.why: MEASURED, four different answers for one model: python keys ['Item'] with required:['name']; php keys ['Item'] but NO required array (Swagger::modelSchema never inspects nullability, so a NOT NULL column is documented optional); ruby emits NO components.schemas at all, so a requestBody degrades to {"type":"object"}; node keys ['items'] - the tableName - so a generated client gets class Items instead of Item. Python is right: the class name is the type name codegen wants, and `required` is what makes the schema worth having. The tina4-nodejs CLAUDE.md claim that models become $ref entries is true but mis-keyed.

invariants.rule: With no TINA4_SWAGGER_* set, info.version, info.description and servers[0].url are identical in all four.
invariants.why: MEASURED, every one differs. info.version: python 1.0.0, php 1.0.0, ruby 3.13.95 (the FRAMEWORK version, so an undocumented app claims API v3.13.95), node 0.0.1. servers[0].url: python and php hard-code http://localhost:7145, ruby and node emit '/'. The hard-coded port is measurably wrong off 7145 - a PHP server bound to 7146 advertised 7145, so Swagger UI 'Try it out' posts to the wrong port. Ruby and Node are right on servers ('/' is correct under any port, host or proxy); Python and PHP are right on version.

invariants.rule: Every documented TINA4_SWAGGER_* variable is read by all four frameworks with the same precedence. A variable documented in one and inert in another is a defect.
invariants.why: MEASURED, all 17 documented vars set to distinctive values in one pass: 15 of 17 matched in every framework. PHP alone ignores TINA4_SWAGGER_CONTACT_TEAM and TINA4_SWAGGER_CONTACT_URL - its info.contact carried only the email while the other three carried name and url. Both are documented in the root and per-framework CLAUDE.md files, so this is drift under the repo's own First Principle. Legacy fallbacks diverge too: SWAGGER_CONTACT_TEAM/_URL are honoured by python and ruby only.

invariants.rule: With TINA4_SWAGGER_ENABLED=false, the UI path, the trailing-slash form, the spec endpoint AND the bundled UI assets all 404, in every framework.
invariants.why: MEASURED and CURRENTLY PASSING in all four, verified against freshly-bound PIDs after a first reading was confounded by a stale process. Written down because it is the production exposure switch and it HAS regressed before - the 3.13.40 static-asset bypass left /swagger/index.html reachable while the gated routes 404'd. A rule that holds today and has broken once is exactly the kind worth pinning.

invariants.rule: Framework-internal routes are excluded from the published document by one shared rule, not a per-framework list.
invariants.why: MEASURED: internal paths documented - python 3, php 13, ruby 3, node 3. PHP additionally publishes /, /ai, /ai/api/chat, /embed, /image, /image/v1/images/generations, /rag, /vision, /__feedback/api/turn and /__feedback/widget.js in the public API document. The exclusion list is /swagger + /__dev in all four; PHP simply registers more internals outside those prefixes. /__feedback/widget.js also yields operationId get___feedback_widget.js - a dot in a generated method name.

invariants.rule: Two distinct paths never collapse to the same operationId, and the same route produces the same id in all four.
invariants.why: MEASURED on /__health versus /health: python and php preserve the leading underscores and produce get___health and get_health; ruby and node collapse both to get_health and de-duplicate the second to get_health_2. operationId is the generated client's METHOD NAME, so this decides what a consumer's SDK calls the endpoint - and which of two endpoints gets the suffix depends on registration order.

invariants.rule: The document reflects a route registered AFTER an earlier fetch to the same running server. The spec re-reads the LIVE route table on every request; it is never a snapshot frozen at server boot.
invariants.why: MEASURED 2026-08-11 (SWAG-NODE-BOOT-SNAPSHOT): Node's swagger routes closed over `const allRoutes = router.getRoutes()`, captured ONCE in server.ts before DevAdmin.register runs, and `getSpec = () => swagger.generate(allRoutes, modelDefs)` reused that frozen array on every request thereafter - the spec regenerated per request, but always over the SAME boot-time route list, so a route added after boot (a hot-reload, or DevAdmin.register itself, which registers AFTER this block) never appeared. Python/PHP/Ruby always re-read the live route table inside generate() and were never the gap. FIXED in Node (tina4-nodejs packages/core/src/server.ts) by reading router.getRoutes() live inside getSpec() and deleting the boot-time capture; proven here by mutation in every framework (Node's case drives a real hot-reload: a route file is dropped after boot and POST /__dev/api/reload registers it on the live router mid-process).

invariants.rule: /__feedback/* is absent from the published document REGARDLESS of registration order or timing - excluded by the shared internal-exclusion RULE, never by an accident of when it happens to be registered relative to the swagger route snapshot.
invariants.why: MEASURED 2026-08-11 (SWAG-NODE-FEEDBACK-LEAK): Node's /__feedback/* IS registered into the main router (feedback.ts registerFeedbackRoutes, called unconditionally at the top of DevAdmin.register) and was kept out of the document ONLY by BOOT ORDERING - the swagger route snapshot (server.ts) predated DevAdmin.register, so /__feedback simply had not been added yet when the (frozen) route list was captured, not because any rule excluded it. Fixing the boot-snapshot invariant above removes that accidental protection, so /__feedback (and the same 8-prefix internal list PHP already carried - /swagger, /__dev, /__feedback, /ai, /rag, /vision, /embed, /image) was added to Node's isIncludedPath exclusion (SWAG-EXCLUSION-NOT-SHARED) - the SAME list python and ruby also widened from /swagger+/__dev only, so one shared rule now backs all four frameworks rather than three different mechanisms. A reorder of DevAdmin.register before the swagger block would previously have published `POST /__feedback/api/turn` as a secured route; it cannot now, proven by mutation (Node: remove /__feedback from the exclusion list with a real TINA4_DEBUG=true server and the route leaks into the real served document).

invariants.rule: A secured operation's `security` requirement, its `401` response, and its `summary`/`tags` are byte-identical across all four frameworks for the same route; an undecorated operation never fabricates a `description`.
invariants.why: MEASURED 2026-08-11 (SWAG-401-SHAPE, SWAG-SHAPE-DRIFT): python emitted NO 401 on a secured operation and omitted summary/tags entirely when undecorated - the odd one out on both counts, since php/ruby/node always populated them. ruby always stamped `description: ""` on every undecorated operation - the odd one out there, since python/php/node only add description when a caller explicitly sets one. Per OWNER-DECISIONS.md (2026-08-11, Batch 4): secured swagger ops document a 401 (python adds it, matching the other three); summary/tags converge on ALWAYS-POPULATE (python now defaults an undecorated operation's summary to `METHOD path` and its tag to the first path segment, matching php/ruby/node's existing fallback); description converges on OMIT-WHEN-UNSET (ruby drops its fabricated empty-string default, matching python/php/node). FIXED in python (tina4_python/swagger/__init__.py) and ruby (lib/tina4/swagger.rb); php and node already matched the converged shape and needed no change. A positive control (a plain secured POST) and a negative control (the same route made explicitly public) both prove summary/tags populate regardless of security while no description is ever fabricated.
